article.title: Everyday phone call phrases
article.description: Answering: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Asking to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' Ending: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Common mistake: 'I am [name]' on the phone sounds unnatural in English — 'This is [name]' is the standard phone convention.
article.content: Answering: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Asking to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' Ending: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Common mistake: 'I am [name]' on the phone sounds unnatural in English — 'This is [name]' is the standard phone convention.

generated.caption:
Ever said "I am [name]" on a phone call and felt it sounded a bit off? 🤔

On the phone, "This is [name] speaking" is the standard and most natural way to introduce yourself! For instance: "Hello, this is Sarah speaking."

To ask someone to wait, say "Could you hold on a second?". And to end a call politely, "Thanks for calling, talk soon!" works perfectly.

Save this for your next call! Follow @TheEnglishVault for daily English tips.
generated.script:
Phone pe bolte time 'I am [name]' bolna thoda weird lagta hai na? Aapne bhi kabhi ye mistake kiya hoga. Toh suno!

Jab bhi phone pe baat karte hain, bohot log bolte hain 'Hello, I am Rohan.' But English mein, ye thoda unnatural sound karta hai. The correct way to answer a call is 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Jaise, 'Hello, this is Riya speaking.' This is the standard phone convention. Agar aapko kisi ko hold pe rakhna hai, you can say 'Could you hold on a second?' Aur jab call finish karna ho, just say 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!'

Ab samajh aaya? Next time phone uthao toh remember: 'This is [name] speaking' hi bolna hai!

Save kar lo ye tips! Aur comment mein batao aapko ye pehle se pata tha ya nahi.

slides.body: When answering a phone call in English, the standard and most natural way to introduce yourself is by saying, 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' It's a common mistake to say, 'I am [name],' but this actually sounds unnatural in English phone conversations. For example, if someone calls for you, you'd answer: 'Hello, this is Sarah speaking.' Remember other useful phrases like 'Could you hold on a second?' if you need a moment, and 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' to end the conversation politely. Mastering these will make your phone calls sound much more natural.
